metadata.name: h200-beauty-studies
metadata.purpose: Unified beauty-studies stack: FLUX Tea surface, governor gateway, and the aesthetic jury models
metadata.note: governor.json on the governor node describes the governor's own deployment, not the beauty stack. The beauty stack's governor posture is declared here and graded against the deployment card.

governor.source: provision_jury.sh, jury_continuum.toml, and the image inventory all name the FP8 build for the H200. Do NOT take this from a governor.json whose card_profile is a100 — that file carries the W4A16 4-bit cut, which exists only because an 80 GiB A100 cannot hold FP8.

coder.source: Verified on the Hub: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 resolves (qwen3_5, image-text-to-text). An earlier note in this file called it fabricated; that was wrong.

knownDefects: GPU fractions are not additive shares: vLLM reads --gpu-memory-utilization as an absolute fraction of the whole card and subtracts memory other processes hold. The shipped 0.40/0.22/0.20 are per-process absolutes, so co-resident servers mis-size and crashloop.
All vLLM programs autostart simultaneously, so each profiles free memory while the others are still allocating. Aux servers must wait for the governor to be healthy.
No model weights baked in and no cache mount, so every container restart re-downloads >100 GiB.
supervisord.conf omits [unix_http_server]/[rpcinterface]/[supervisorctl], so supervisorctl cannot connect and the entrypoint's shutdown trap can never fire.
Tea is served with --unsafe-no-auth bound to 0.0.0.0.
NOT a defect (verified 2026-08-20): the lowercased repo id redhatai/gemma-4-31b-it-fp8-dynamic resolves fine; the Hub 307-redirects to the canonical casing.

deployment.note: The beauty stack runs on the H200 deploy node. The local a100 box is the governor's own card (see ~/.gemstone/governor.json, card_profile a100) and is not a beauty target; do not grade the beauty VRAM budget against it.
